alex: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection flip we see a big cold-path regression on private/VPC clusters. p95 shot up.
priya: which percentiles / workloads?
alex: short prompts (<64 tokens). p95 went from ~120ms -> ~420ms on private nodes. hosted + dedicated unchanged.
mike: any KV hit-rate numbers?
alex: yes — KV prefix hit dropped from 78% -> 12% on private. hosted still ~75%.
sara: so this is a cache miss storm on netstore paths?
alex: looks like it. profile traces show a lot more small RPCs to the network cache, plus extra serialization steps.
perf-bot: Profiling summary (thread 1870012345): workload=short prompts, before: KV_hit=78%, avg_token_latency=12ms; after: private_KV_hit=14%, hosted_KV_hit=75%; RPCs per request +2.8x; likely cause: cache key serialization mismatch after kernel switch.
priya: kernel selection changed anything in key generator or serialization format?
mike: the kernel switch included a bundled runtime change that tightened cross-language structures; it swapped our key hashing helper to the new `hashed_v2` path.
alex: trace shows generated key includes a newline separator now ("sha256(prefix + \n + normalized_prompt)") whereas earlier it was concatenated without newline. netstore normalizes / strips line endings, so keys don't match.
sara: ah — hosted uses local memstore so it survived; private netstore normalization caused the miss.
priya: immediate mitigations?
alex: 1) rollback kernel flag on private clusters, 2) set compatibility env var to accept legacy keys, 3) run a targeted warmup of top prefixes.
sara: sample config that caused mismatch: ```yaml
cache:
  key_format: "hashed_v2"
  serialize: "msgpack"
  sync_mode: "async"
```
mike: repro steps I ran: 1) send 5k short prompts to private cluster; 2) capture cache keys from runtime and compare to netstore canonical keys; 3) observe mismatch in delimiting byte.
priya: quick warmup script idea: fetch top-k prefixes from metrics and prefetch in parallel. pseudo: ```bash
curl -H \"Auth: token\" https://metrics/api/top_prefixes | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -sS -XPOST https://cache.local/warm?key={}
```
perf-bot: Warmup simulation for top-100 prefixes improves hit-rate on startup from ~15% -> ~65% in our test harness (approx).
infra-bot: Rollback job queued for private clusters: job_id=rb-187001-9, ETA ~8m.
mike: followups: add unit tests that assert identical key bytes across codepaths (hosted/dedicated/private) and fuzz whitespace, newline, unicode normalization.
sara: long-term: canonicalize key serializer independent of kernel flags, add an acceptance test that runs against a netstore emulator in CI.
priya: I'll open a PR with a normalization shim and the rollout playbook (env var + phased rollback + warmup) and link perf numbers.
alex: TL;DR — regression due to key serialization change after kernel selection; immediate: rollback private flag + set CACHE_ACCEPT_LEGACY; medium: warmup top prefixes; long: serializer unification + tests.
priya: thanks — assigning myself to the PR and the CI job. :thumbsup:
